units: <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 36a:5">Ab. Zar. 36ᵃ</cite> <he>שמלאי ל׳ קאמרת</he> thou citest Samlai, the Lyddan; (Y. ib. II, 41ᵈ bot. <he>הדרומי</he>).—
<cite ref="Yevamot 71b:2">Yeb. 71ᵇ</cite>, v. preced.—Pl. <he>לוּדָאֵי</he>. Ab. Zar. l. c. <he>שאני ל׳ דמזלזלי</he> it is different with Lyddan scholars, because they disregard traditional laws.

senses.gloss: לוּדָאֵי (denom. of ludi, the latter being treated as a geographical term) people hiring men for gladiatorial contests, lanistae (v. Sm. Ant. s. v. Gladiator).
units: Gitt. 46ᵇ bot. ההוא גברא דזבין נפשיה לל׳ there was the case of a man who had sold himself to the Ludaë.
<cite ref="Gittin 47a:4">Ib. 47ᵃ</cite> <he>ריש לקיש</he> … <he>לל׳</he> Resh Lakish had sold himself &c.—

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 8:3:16">Y. Ter. VIII, 45ᵈ</cite> top <he>אילו זבנת גרמך ללוּדָנִין הות מזבין וכ׳</he> (not <he>הוה</he>; prob. to be read: <cite ref="L00203"><he>לוּדָיִין</he></cite>) if thou hadst sold thyself to the lanistae, thou wouldst have sold (thyself) at a high price, but here thou hast sold (risked) thy life for a trifle.—V. <cite ref="L00199"><he>לוּדִים</he></cite>.
